rows.grounds: compound of ānanda (bliss) and cakra (circle), object of declaration
temporal marker indicating transition to exposition
demonstrative compound pointing to the specific bliss-circle to be expounded
first-person plural statement of intent to expound

items.question: Which specific bliss-circle is now set forth for exposition?
premises: The discourse marks a transition to a new topic now.
That very bliss-circle is identified as the object of exposition.
The speakers commit to declaring this bliss-circle.
items.inference: Therefore the exposition now turns to that specific bliss-circle.
uncertainties: The precise referent of the bliss-circle depends on the preceding and following context.
items.plain_english: Now we declare that very circle of bliss.
